pages.text: Where is Sam?
Sam is up.
Where is Sam?
Sam is down.
Where is Sam?
Sam is in.
Where is Sam?
Sam is out.
Where is Sam?
Sam is here!
This is for Mom.
Here is a basket.
This is for Mom.
Here is tea.
This is for Mom.
Here is a cup.
This is for Mom.
Here is a hat.
This is for Mom.
Here is a hug!
Oh no, the tea!
Oh no, the cup!
Oh no, the cake!
Oh no, the chair!
Oh no, the hat!
Oh no, the bag!
Oh no, the note!
Oh no, the mess!
It is okay.
The dragon can help!
What do you see?
I see a city.
What do you see?
I see the moon.
What do you see?
I see a dragon.
What do you see?
I see a robot.
What do you see?
I see my room!
It is too hot.
Make it cold!
It is too cold.
Make it wet!
It is too wet.
Make it dry!
It is too dry.
Make it calm!
It is a rainbow!
It is just right!
A cook is here.
A nurse is here.
A driver is here.
A farmer is here.
A pilot is here.
A teacher is here.
A baker is here.
A doctor is here.
A builder is here.
We are all here!
This sign says stop.
This sign says yield.
This sign says cross.
This sign says children.
This sign says light.
This sign says one way.
This sign says no.
This sign says walk.
This sign says bikes.
This sign says train!
This is a phone.
This is a laptop.
This is a tablet.
This is a charger.
This is a headset.
This is a robot.
This is a drone.
This is a battery.
This is a screen.
This is a camera!
This was a river.
This was a mountain.
This was a forest.
This was a desert.
This was an ocean.
This was an island.
This was a bridge.
This was a city.
What is this?
It is a seed!
Pip is a little duck.
Pip wants to swim.
Pip sees the water.
Pip sees the ducks.
The water is cold.
Pip puts one foot in the water.
The water feels nice.
Pip goes in the water.
Pip sinks!
Mom duck helps.
Pip loves the water!
Mia has a little fish.
The fish is yellow.
Mia taps the glass.
The fish swims to Mia.
Mia gives the fish food.
The fish eats and eats.
The fish grows and grows.
The fish is too big.
Mia thinks.
Mia takes the fish to a big bowl.
Zed is a small robot.
A cat scares Zed.
Night comes.
Zed hears a small sound.
Zed looks in the dark.
The cat is stuck in a tree.
Zed helps the cat.
The cat purrs.
Zed feels very happy.
Zed is a brave robot.
Zed and the cat play.
Pat is a little snail.
Pat is slow.
Pat races a fast rat.
He loses.
Pat races a toad.
He loses.
Pat races a beetle.
He loses.
Pat races an ant.
He loses.
Pat races a fly.
He loses.
Pat races a water bear.
He wins!
A kitten is lost.
The kitten cries and cries.
Ben sees the kitten.
He grabs the kitten.
The kitten bites.
Ben is a little mad.
The kitten is very sad.
Ben takes the kitten home.
Mom takes care of Ben.
Ben thinks.
Ben gives the kitten milk.
The kitten is happy.
Goodbye trees, hello yellow hay.
Sheep eat hay.
Sheep fart.
Oh no, gas!
Goodbye trees, hello sweet corn.
Pigs eat corn.
Pigs burp.
Oh no, gas!
Goodbye trees, hello green grass.
Cows eat grass.
Cows fart.
Cows burp.
Oh no, gas!
Earth is so hot.
The robot cook makes food.
The robot nurse helps sick people.
The robot driver takes us places.
The robot teacher helps us learn.
The robot farmer grows our food.
The robot baker makes bread.
The robot doctor helps us stay well.
The robot builder makes houses.
The robot pilot flies.
What job can I do?
I hate the rain.
I love the rain.
I hate the sunshine.
I love the sunshine.
I hate the snow.
I love the snow.
I hate the wind.
I love the wind.
I hate the fog.
I love the fog.
I hate the smog.
Me too!
Lin sits at her little desk.
Lin wants her little pencil.
Lin looks in her little bag.
The little pencil is not there.
Lin looks on the little desk.
Lin looks on the floor.
Lin looks in a little book.
Lin looks in her hair.
The pencil is in her hair!
Lin grins at the little pencil.
Lin writes in the little book.
Lin writes a little line.
Lin holds up the little pencil!
Lin can write a little more.
Kip has a little red ball.
Kip wants to kick it.
Kip kicks the red ball hard.
The red ball goes in a tree.
Kip looks up at the tree.
Dad gets the little red ball.
Dad says, "Kick it soft."
Kip kicks the red ball soft.
The red ball goes to Dad.
Dad kicks it to Kip.
Kip kicks it to the net!
The red ball is in the net!
Kip and Dad jump up!
They grin at the red ball.
Jen walks in the sun.
A little cloud follows Jen.
The little cloud sits on Jen.
The little cloud drips on Jen.
Jen looks up at the cloud.
Jen says, "Do not drip!"
The little cloud drips and drips.
Jen laughs at the little cloud.
Jen holds out a little hand.
The little cloud sits in it.
A little rainbow pops up!
Jen grins at the little cloud.
Sun shines on the rainbow.
Jen and the little cloud walk on.
Oli has a new little watch.
The new watch can beep.
Mom sets the new watch.
Oli plays with a little red truck.
The new watch beeps at Oli.
Oli looks at the new watch.
Mom says, "Time to go!"
Oli puts the little truck down.
Oli puts on his little bag.
Oli runs to the little door.
Mom grins at little Oli.
Oli grins at the new watch.
Oli pats the new watch.
Beep! Oli and Mom go out!
See this little brown seed.
The little seed is in a cup.
Water goes in the little cup.
The sun is on the little cup.
The little seed gets wet.
The little seed gets sun.
A little brown root comes out.
The little root goes down.
A little green tip pops up.
The green tip is a plant.
The little plant wants sun.
The little plant wants water.
A new green leaf pops up!
Look at the little green plant!
See this hard little corn.
The hard corn is in a pot.
The big pot gets very hot.
The hard little corn gets hot.
Pop! The corn gets big.
Pop! Pop! More corn pops.
The big hot pot is full.
The big corn is white.
The white corn is soft.
The hot corn is in a bowl.
Take a little hot white bite.
The hot white corn is good!
Crunch! Crunch! Eat more corn!
The bowl has more hot corn!
See this little Zip bot.
Little Zip is on the floor.
Little Zip goes beep beep.
Zip eats dust on the little floor.
Little Zip hits a chair.
Little Zip turns and goes.
Little Zip eats more little dust.
Zip goes to its little bed.
Little Zip sits in the bed.
Zip's little light goes off.
The floor is so clean.
Little Zip can rest in bed.
Zip rests in the little bed.
Beep. Little Zip is still in bed.
See this little red magnet.
The little red magnet can pull.
It pulls a little red pin.
The little pin sticks on.
It pulls a little red clip.
The little clip sticks on.
It does not pull a little cup.
The cup does not stick.
It pulls a little red spoon.
The little spoon sticks on!
The pin is on the red magnet.
The clip is on the magnet.
Look at the spoon stick!
The red magnet pulls a pile!

Hana sits with Mom
at the table.
Mom holds the tablet.

Hana taps Nana's face.
Nana grins on the tablet.
Mom holds it still.

Nana waves at Hana.
Hana waves at Nana
on the tablet.

"I made a sun,"
says Hana.
She holds the sun up.

Hana holds the sun
up to Nana on the tablet.
Nana grins at the sun.

Nana holds a sun too.
It's the same sun!
They grin at the suns.

"We made the same sun!"
says Nana.
Hana claps at the tablet.

Nana puts her sun
on her fridge.
The sun sticks on it.

Hana puts her sun
on her fridge too.
Two suns sit on two fridges.

Hana grins at Nana.
Nana grins at Hana.
The tablet stays on.

Nana blows a kiss
to Hana on the tablet.
The kiss flies at the glass.

The kiss hits the glass!
Hana kisses the glass too.
A mark sits on the tablet.

Luis looks at the helmet.
Dad set it on the porch.
The helmet is open.

A bird looks in the helmet.
The helmet is open.
Luis grins at the bird.

The bird brings a stick.
She drops the stick
in the helmet.

She brings more sticks.
A nest sits in Dad's helmet.
Luis does not touch the nest.

Dad wants his helmet.
He wants to ride his bike.
The helmet's not on the hook.

"Where is my helmet?"
says Dad.
Luis looks at the porch.

Luis points at the porch.
The helmet is sitting there.
Dad looks at the nest.

Dad picks the helmet up.
A bird sits in Luis's nest!
Dad jumps back from it.

Luis laughs at Dad.
Dad sets the helmet down.
The bird flaps at Dad.

Luis waves at Dad.
Dad can still ride
on the skateboard.

Look in the nest.
Two eggs sit in the sticks
in the helmet.

One egg has a crack!
A beak taps the egg in the nest.
The nest stays on the porch.

Amara looks at the glass.
It is picture day at school.
She wants to look good.

She puts her hair down.
The hair sits there.
She grins at her hair.

She looks in the glass.
The hair pops up!
She pushes the hair down.

Amara walks to the hall.
Kids are in a line.
She stands in the line.

A camera sits on a box.
Amara sits by the camera.
A man looks at the camera.

"Smile for the photo,"
says the man.
Amara grins at the camera.

She sits up on the chair.
Her hair pops up again!
She pushes the hair down.

Flash! The light pops.
Amara looks at the light.
The camera prints
out a photo.

The photo comes out
of the camera.
Amara looks at the photo.

The pop is in the photo.
Her hair is crazy in the photo.
Amara laughs at the photo.

The man laughs with her.
Amara takes the photo home.
She puts the photo on the shelf.

Mom grins at the photo.
The hair pops in the photo!
It's Amara's look.

Asha wants to hide.
Dad will look for her.
He shuts his eyes.

"Go hide,"
says Dad.
Asha runs down the hall to hide.

Asha looks in the bath.
It's no good to hide.
She runs on.

She looks in the laundry.
A basket is sitting there.
The lid is open.

Asha gets in the basket.
She pulls the lid down.
It's dark in the basket.

Dad looks in the bath.
He does not see Asha in it.
He looks by the bed.

The dog sits by the basket.
His nose is on the lid.
Asha is in the basket.

Dad walks by the basket.
He does not look in it.
The dog barks at the lid.

The dog barks at the lid.
The lid pops up
on Asha's head!

"I see you, Asha!"
says Dad.
Asha pops out of the basket.

Dad hides by the curtain.
His big feet stick out of it!
Asha sees Dad's feet.

The dog gets in the basket.
The lid sits on his tail!
Asha laughs at the dog.

Eva sits up in bed.
The room is dark.
She looks at the door.

A dark shape stands
by the door in the room.
Eva's eyes get wide.

"That is a monster!"
says Eva.
She looks at the shape.

Eva turns on the lamp.
Light hits the dark shape by the door.
The shape is a coat.

The shape is a coat.
The coat hangs by the door.
Eva grins at the coat.

She turns off the lamp.
The room is dark
by the coat.

The coat moves in the dark room.
It looks big by the door.
Eva sits up in bed.

Eva taps the lamp on.
The coat is just Eva's coat!
A hat sits on the coat.

The hat is Eva's hat.
It sits on the coat.
Eva laughs at the hat.

She puts the hat on.
The coat hangs by the door
in the dark room.

Eva turns off the lamp.
A star glows by the bed.
The coat hangs still.

The coat lifts a bit!
It's just the wind.
Eva sleeps in her hat.

Mina looks at the window.
Rain hits the glass.
She wants the park.

The rain comes down
on the park.
Mina sits at the window.

"No park today,"
says Dad.
Mina looks at the pillows.

Mina takes a pillow.
She sets it on the rug.
She takes more pillows.

The pillows make a fort.
Mina gets in the fort.
It's warm in the fort.

Dad looks at the fort.
He gets in with a pillow.
It's a fort for two.

Dad puts a pillow
on the fort.
The fort gets big.

Mina laughs in the fort.
Dad laughs with her.
The fort falls!

Dad is in the pillows
on the rug.
Pillows hit the rug.

Dad's hands pop out!
Mina looks at the hands.
Dad pops up.

Mina pulls the pillows off.
Dad sits on the rug.
A pillow sits on top
of his head.

Mina laughs at Dad.
The pillow hat is on!
The rain hits the glass.

Look at this dish.
Put water in the dish.
The water sits still.

Shake pepper on the water.
The pepper sits on top of it.
It does not sink.

Tap the dish a bit.
The pepper still sits
on the water.

Get a drop of soap.
Hold it on a finger.
Don't drop the soap yet.

The drop hits the water.
It hits the middle of the dish.
Watch the pepper on top.

The pepper runs!
It runs to the sides.
The middle is open.

See the open middle.
The soap did that.
The pepper runs from the soap.

Put a paper boat on.
The boat is small.
It's a paper boat.

Add a soap drop
by the paper boat.
The boat will run.

The boat shoots off!
It runs to the side of the dish.
Pepper runs with the boat.

The boat runs to
the edge of the dish.
It stops at the rim.

Pepper sits on the sides.
The boat sits at the edge.
The boat ran away!

You sit at a table.
A man brings water.
There is no paper menu.

Look at the table.
A black square sits
on the table.

The square has little dots.
You look at the dots.
It sits by the cups.

You point your phone
at the black square.
The phone looks at the dots.

Hot food pops on the phone.
You can see the noodles.
You tap the noodles.

The phone beeps again.
A man brings a bowl.
The bowl has the noodles.

You eat the hot noodles.
They are so good.
The black square still sits on it.

The square still sits
on the table.
It did not go away.

You tap the black square
again.
The food pops up again!

That square was the menu!
It's not a paper menu.
The phone did the work.

You know the trick.
You can get the menu again.
Just tap the square.

Tap the square for fun.
The menu pops up again!
You grin at the trick.

Look at this bag.
A bar sits in the bag.
The bag is shut.

The bag sits in the sun.
The bag gets hot in the sun.
The bar sits in the bag.

Open the bag.
The bar is mush.
It's not a bar.

The bar is mush.
You can't eat this mush
in the bag.

Get a new bag.
Put in a cold pack.
The pack is cold.

Put in a new bar.
Shut the bag on the bar.
The cold pack sits in the bag.

The bag sits in the sun.
The cold pack sits in it
with the bar.

Open the bag.
The bar is hard.
The pack is wet.

The cold pack keeps
the bar hard in the bag.
This bar can snap.

Hold the hard bar.
Snap! The bar is in two.
It's hard all the way.

You can eat this bar.
It's not mush.
The cold pack did it.

The old mush sits
in a dish. A fly sits on it!
Don't eat that mush.

Stand at the curb.
Cars go by fast.
Don't step out yet.

See the walk button
on the pole.
It's by the street.

Press the button.
A click comes from the button.
Look at the sign.

A stop hand is on.
Wait at the curb.
Don't walk yet.

Cars go by the curb.
The stop hand stays on.
You still wait at the curb.

A walk man is on.
You can walk.
Look at the cars.

Walk on the white lines.
A dog walks on the lines too.
The cars have to stop.

Get to the side.
The stop hand is back.
Cars go by.

A new button sits
on this side.
Don't press this button.

Stay on this side.
The dog does not stay here.
The dog goes to the pole.

The dog looks at the button.
His nose is on the button.
Then a paw goes up.

The dog hits
the walk button
with a paw too!

Lina stands on a wooden stool
in the yellow kitchen.
Mom cuts green limes
beside a bowl of red salsa.

Lina points at the floor
by the white fridge.
One last lime sits there,
and she grins.

Up on the stool,
Lina holds the lime
high in both hands.
Her smile is huge.

Nico holds up a spoon.
Red salsa dots his chin
and his green shirt.
He looks up at Lina.

Mom rubs her tired face.
Steam rises from a pot
of rice on the stove.

Nico's lip wobbles.
He reaches up with both hands
for the lime Lina holds.

Lina sets the last lime
into Nico's small hands.
He smiles and holds it close.

Nico laughs and rolls the lime
on the floor near the fridge.
Coco the cat watches,
and her long tail flicks.

Lina stirs the salsa
from the top of the stool.
Mom sits in the chair
and smiles.

Mom tastes the salsa
from a spoon.
Lina looks at Nico.
He still holds the lime.

Nico hugs the lime
and shakes his head.
Lina keeps stirring the bowl
and leaves the lime with him.

The lime slips and rolls
to the white fridge.
Coco bats it underneath
and dives after it.
Nico gasps.
Mina runs across the green grass at the city park. Her red shirt and black shorts stand out in the sun, and a black soccer ball stays right at her feet.
June waits by the white goal in a red shirt, both arms up. "Kick it here!" he calls, as Mina runs in with the ball.
Mina kicks the black ball hard. It flies past June and the white goal, heading for the fence.
The black ball lands on a picnic blanket by the dirt path. A dad in a blue shirt looks up from his chips, grapes, and sandwich.
Chips, red grapes, and bits of sandwich fly off the blanket. The dad leans back on the grass. "That was my lunch!"
Mina stands by the picnic with a hot pink face. She looks down at the grapes spilled on the blanket, and at the black ball sitting in the mess.
"I am sorry I hit your lunch," said Mina. The dad looks at her and smiles a little.
June sets the black ball on the grass beside Mina. The picnic dad watches them from his blanket by the path.
By the white goal, June points at the ball. "Can you pass it?" he asks. Mina looks right at him.
Mina kicks a soft pass across the green grass. The black ball floats toward June, and he runs to meet it by the white goal.
The ball is in the net. Mina and June jump by the white goal with their arms up, and the picnic dad claps from his blanket.
A brown duck walks off with a big bun from the picnic. The black ball lies on the grass with mustard on it.

A wet log sits on the dirt.
In the dark space under it, a pink worm peeks out.

A pink worm slides through the wet soil under the log.
Damp brown leaves lie close beside it.

A shiny black beetle grips a dry brown leaf.
It tugs the leaf along in the shade under the log.

Gray roly-polies curl into tight little balls.
They sit on the damp dirt beside the wet log.

A brown slug creeps along the wet bark.
It leaves a shiny silver trail behind it.

A long orange centipede runs on many legs.
It hurries across the dark dirt under the log.

A small orange salamander sits in the cool mud under the log.
Its skin looks wet in the shade.

Black ants follow a thin path in the dirt.
They carry crumbs toward a small hole by the log.

Sunlight warms the top of the log.
Underneath, a worm and a roly-poly rest in the deep shade.

Dead brown leaves lie beside the rotting log.
A bright green sprout pushes up from the dark soil.

Two hands set the wet log back down on the dirt.
The dark space under it is covered again.

The old log is crumbling, and tiny bugs fill the soft wood.
A young green sprout rises beside it.

A duck walks through the muddy bakery door.
Its webbed feet leave prints in the spilled flour.

A farmer in tall boots carries hay across the wet field.
The cows crowd the gate and wait.

A mail carrier holds her bag up over a puddle.
The cart waits on the wet street, and the letters stay dry.

A plumber lies under the kitchen sink.
Water drips into her bucket while she works on the pipe.

A sweeper pushes wet leaves to the curb.
Brown water runs off the street, and two kids step around the pile.

A washer holds a soapy brown pup.
The pup shakes, and suds spray her shirt.

A cook mops the slick kitchen floor.
Pans steam on the stove behind him.

A bus driver holds the rail and smiles at a boy.
He stands on the wet steps and holds on too.

A nurse hands dry socks to a boy in the clinic chair.
He grins at the fresh pair.

A builder sets a post in the mud.
The wooden fence beside him leans to one side.

At dusk, muddy boots drip on a wooden rack.
Little cakes of mud dry on the floor.

One clean boot sits by the night door.
A frog peeks from the muddy one.
Snacks cover the long lunch table in a big mixed pile. Kids lean in, point, and grin.
A yellow banana rolls off a shiny blue plate, bumps a candy bar, and stops.
Small hands peel a ripe yellow banana beside an open lunch box.
A white cup of yogurt sits in a small bowl of ice. It looks cool and thick.
A cup of yogurt and cubes of yellow cheese share one snack plate.
Hands snap a crisp orange carrot in half. A bitten red apple drips juice right beside it.
Brown nuts fill a small red cup on the lunch table.
A shiny candy bar lies unwrapped beside a kid who sits looking tired.
Two friends swap snacks across the long lunch table. A bag of chips goes one way, and a green pear comes the other.
A kid bites the green pear and smiles wide. Juice runs down a chin and a hand.
A cup of cold water sits by the leftover snacks, with ice still in it.
An empty snack box sits open on the long lunch table.
A tall black gate stands open at the city park. Beside it, a map on a post shows a blue pond, green trees, and a brown path.
Bright swings stand in the grass. A path runs from them to a picnic lawn, where a checkered blanket and a basket sit under one big shady tree.
A tiny park hides between two brick shops. One wooden bench faces a small map, with red, yellow, and purple flowers in front.
A wide trail starts at a wooden post. The map on the post shows two green hills and a small blue creek.
The play park has bright blue swings and one tall yellow slide. A map on a pole shows the water fountain that stands beside it.
Two white ducks swim on the city park pond. A sign on the wooden rail shows a piece of bread with a red X.
Two families share one long picnic table in the shade. They move their bags so a new family can sit with them.
A worker picks paper cups off the path with a long grabber. Two kids drop apple peels into a bin next to the map.
Soft rain dots the wet park map by the iron gate. Two people still walk the long path under one tree, sharing a red and yellow umbrella.
A beach park sits on the warm sand. Its map shows a snack hut and a tall red lifeguard chair, and both stand right there by the water.
Two kids walk the barn path at the farm park. They see two brown goats, and the map marks that path and a wide pumpkin patch.
A quiet town park sits beside the water. The map shows a wooden dock and a green hill far away.
Rain taps the red roof. The street below shines with water. Puddles sit in the road and catch the gray sky.
Rain falls from gray clouds. The drops hit the green trees and the parked cars. Water beads on the hoods.
A child stands in the open doorway. A yellow rain hat and tall boots are on, and one hand reaches for a yellow coat. Rain falls on the street outside.
The child stands on the wet sidewalk and looks down. Rain falls around the yellow hat and coat. Tall boots stand in a puddle, and both hands stay in the pockets.
A brown dog steps into a puddle on the park path. Water splashes up from a paw. The fur is wet from the rain.
Two kids in yellow coats jump a wide puddle on the sidewalk. Water flies up in a splash. They laugh as they jump.
A deep dark puddle sits on the park path. The kids walk around it. Their yellow boots stay on the wet edge.
Rain falls on the little garden. Grass and green leaves shine with water. The soil under them is dark and wet.
A yellow bus stops in the rain. One child climbs the steps. Other kids sit inside, and drops blur the windows.
The rain slows down. Drops turn small and soft. Puddles still sit on the street and on the park path.
The sun peeks through a thin break in the gray clouds. The kids tip their yellow rain hats and look up. Warm light finds their faces.
Wet leaves stick to the steps and the street. Wind tugs the yellow rain hat, and the brim lifts. The child stands in the breeze.

A white duck stands in the bike lane.
Two bikes roll up behind it, and kids on the sidewalk stare.

Two riders ring their bike bells on the path by the park.
The duck waddles ahead in the wet lane.

A red scooter slides past the duck.
The rider squeezes a tiny horn, and the duck sits in the lane.

A yellow bus hisses and stops at the curb.
Kids look out the windows and laugh at the duck.

Cars wait in a long line.
A yellow taxi gives one short honk, and the duck sits in the dust.

A brown delivery van turns slowly around the duck.
The driver grins and waves.

A long train rolls over the bridge.
The street and the bike lane stay busy below.

A small green ferry blows its horn on the river.
The duck turns its head toward the water.

A plane climbs over the town.
The duck stares at the street and does not look up.

Bikes, a bus, and a van all go around the duck.
It stands in the lane while they pass.

A worker in a bright vest points to the grass.
The duck hops onto the grass, and the bikes roll by.

The ferry ramp drops down.
One duck waddles onto the boat, and another duck steps into the lane.
A pocket buzzes on the sidewalk. The child in the thick green coat stops and stares down, eyes wide.
It is a phone. The child pulls it from the coat pocket and looks at the bright screen.
At the bus stop, a man checks the watch on his wrist. The small screen glows while he waits.
A tablet sits in an open bag on the bus seat. The map shows streets, a blue river, and a green park.
The clerk taps a tablet at the food shop. Milk, bread, and a jar of red jam sit on the counter.
A cook reads a tablet by the stove. Steam from the soup pot fogs the screen a little.
In the green park, a runner checks her watch and grins.
The dentist holds a tablet by the chair. Two kids lean in to see the bright tooth on the screen.
On the sidewalk, people look down at their phones. Cars wait at the corner, but nobody looks up.
A child looks up at the crosswalk. The phone stays in a pocket, and a blue bike is in the street.
Two kids sit on the couch. One passes the tablet so both of them can see the screen.
A phone, a watch, and a tablet sit beside an open book.
A chip bag lies on the park grass. A duck pecks the shiny bag, and the kids stop to look.
A green park bin stands by the wide path. Kids walk past, with grass and trees behind them.
You carry the chip bag over to the park bin. The lid is open wide.
You drop the bag in, and the lid swings shut. Ants crawl along the rim.
A park worker tips a green bin into a big truck by the gate.
Cans go in the blue bin, paper goes in the green bin, and food scraps go in the brown bin.
A glass bottle lies on the bike path, and a bike wheel swerves around it.
A squirrel in the bush holds a plastic cup and looks surprised.
People at a picnic on the grass drop their plates into the park bin.
A dog on a leash walks the path. A person drops a little dog bag into the bin.
Ducks swim on the still pond and nibble bread crumbs in the clear water.
A raccoon pops out of the bin, holding a cup like a prize, and the lid pinches his tail.

A red hat sits on a sunny fence.
Its shadow on the grass looks like a giant bug.
A blue bird sits on the rail.

The sun shines on the red hat.
The hat blocks the light, so a dark shadow sits on the grass.

Hands slide the red hat to the left.
The shadow slides left across the grass with it.

The sun is high, so the shadow stays short and fat.
Two kids step right over it.

The sun sits low in the sky.
The shadow grows long and thin, like a snake on the grass.

A small lamp glows in a dark bedroom.
Hands hold a cup close to the light, and its shadow falls on the wall.

The cup blocks the lamp light.
A funny cup shadow sits on the wall by the bed.

A tall tree makes a dark shadow on the path.
Two birds hop on a branch, but the shadow stays still.

In the dark, no shadow sits on the floor.
A hand turns the lamp on, and a shadow pops up.

Moonlight makes a pale shadow of the hat and fence on the snow.
The shadow slides slowly across the yard.

The red hat is back in the bright sun.
Light stops at the hat, and a dark shadow sits on the grass.

The sun drops low, and the long shadow slides over the grass.
A bird hops on the fence, and its tiny shadow hops too.
Two kids walked a dirt path, each with a wooden pail. Water splashed from the full pails as they went.
A round stone well sat in the grass. Someone turned the wooden crank, and a bucket hung from the rope.
Kids knelt by the river and dipped clay jugs into the water. One jug tipped, and a splash jumped back out.
At home, the water sat in a big clay pot. A cup hung on a peg beside the window.
In the yard, a mom stirred a pot over a fire. One child poured a pail into a wooden tub, and another child held a pail.
A hand pump stood in front of the house. A child pushed the long handle down, and water ran into a wooden pail.
A child turns a metal tap. Water runs into a bright white sink.
Blue pipes run under the street and off toward the houses. A worker in a yellow hard hat stands beside an open hole.
The tap still drips. One drop falls into the sink, and another drop hangs on the spout.
On a dry, dusty road, two kids pull a wooden cart packed with yellow cans. A blue tap stand stands behind them.
A grownup and a child stand in a grassy yard by an old stone well. A wooden crank rises over the stones.
At the sink, a child holds a small cup of water in both hands.
The lunch bell rings, and kids race into the hall. Steam curls up from the bowls on the long wooden tables.
In Japan, lunch rides on a tray: rice, a piece of fish, and a bowl of soup. Kids carry it to a low table and sit with their friends.
In Mexico, a warm tortilla scoops up beans and salsa. A bright green lime waits on the tray.
In Kenya, ugali makes a soft round heap beside a pile of greens. Kids pinch a bite with clean fingers.
In India, kids pop open stacked tiffin boxes of rice, dal, and pickle. They trade bites and laugh.
In Italy, long pasta fills a deep dish under yellow cheese. Kids twirl the hot noodles on their forks.
In Vietnam, kids lean over big bowls and slurp noodle soup. Herbs and a squeeze of lime sit on top.
In Peru, kids share roasted corn and potatoes in the open air. They grin while the corn is still hot.
Some lunches come in bags from home. Some come ladled from the big school pots. Kids wait in a long, cheerful line.
Before anyone eats, hands go under the tap. Kids scrub with soap until the bubbles cover their fingers.
Lunch is done, and the kids burst into the yard. They run, and nobody wants to stand still.
Every bowl on the table is empty. The kids are on their feet, talking with their friends.

Two kids sit at the lunch table.
One slaps the wood with an open hand.
The other holds a cup so it will not tip.

Jamal reaches fast for the orange cat.
The cat ducks under the chair.

Mei holds a baby on the couch.
The baby's head tips back, so Mei puts one hand on the baby's back.

Tess works with wet clay at the art table.
One hand smacks a clay face flat.
Her other palm stays soft on the next ball.

At the classroom sink, Luis picks up a wet cup.
It slides, so he grips it with both hands.

A girl sits on the hard playground and holds her stinging knee.
A boy holds out his hand.

Kids sit in a circle and pass a picture book.
One boy yanks the book.
The girl beside him slides it to a friend.

One small scene shows a boy reaching for the cat.
One shows a hand on a baby's back.
One shows a soft pat on a clay ball.
One shows a boy helping a friend stand.

At home, a boy washes a plate at the sink.
At school, a girl holds scissors by the finger holes, and the pointy tips face down.

A dog jumps up in the yard.
The kids keep their hands low and let the dog sniff.

A boy slaps the lunch table.
In the next picture, two slow fingers pat the orange cat, and the cat stays close.

The orange cat steps out from under the chair.
Jamal sits with his fingers waiting on his knee.
The cat steps closer.

Malik sits on the brown couch in his green hoodie.
Grandpa sits beside him in a blue sweater.
They look at the wooden radio on the shelf.
The dials are dark. The radio is quiet.

Malik leans close and shouts into the speaker.
"Hello? Can you hear me?"
Grandpa laughs on the couch
and wipes his glasses on his sweater.

Grandpa turns the silver knob.
Malik taps the top of the radio.
They wait.
The radio stays quiet.

Malik opens the kitchen drawer.
Keys, tape, and a bent spoon spill out.
He digs through the pile.
There are no batteries.

Mom stands in the doorway in a yellow shirt,
a laundry basket in her arms.
Malik's shoulders drop.
The open drawer still has no batteries.

Malik checks the bathroom shelf.
Only a folded towel is up there.
Grandpa looks inside the lamp by the couch.
Still no batteries.

Out on the sunny porch, the radio sits on the table.
Malik holds up a little blue case.
Grandpa sets his hands on his hips and looks.

Malik sits on the couch and looks down
at his red toy car on the rug.
Grandpa stands by the radio,
one hand on his chin.

Malik pops open the little door on the toy car.
Two batteries sit in his hand.
"Try these," he says.
Grandpa watches.

The radio glows on the shelf.
Malik and Grandpa lean in close.
They wear the same wide grin.

Malik taps a beat on Grandpa's knee.
Grandpa smiles and taps back.
The red toy car sits still on the rug.

A sparrow lands on the window sill.
Malik points and whispers, "Look."
Grandpa watches the bird from the couch.

The sparrow hops on the sill.
Malik and Grandpa sit very still and watch it bounce.
The radio glows behind them.

Malik stands on the rec court under the high orange rim.
He holds the orange ball in both hands.
His white shoes rest on the warm cement.

Tia sits on the low wall beside the court.
She holds her water and looks toward the hoop.
The orange rim is high above the cement.

Malik jumps and lifts the orange ball toward the high rim.
Tia stays on the low wall and watches him shoot.

The orange ball sits in Rosa's tomato pots.
Dirt dots the ball.
Rosa stands by the plants with a green hose.

Malik reaches over the low fence for the dirty ball.
Rosa watches from the pots, the hose still in her hand.

Tia dribbles the orange ball on the cement.
She keeps the bounce low, right by her white shoes.
Malik stands beside her and watches.

Malik bends down and bounces the ball with both hands.
Tia bends with him, one hand on the ball.
It taps the cement in a soft beat.

Tia bounces the orange ball toward Malik.
The pass stays low, close to her knee.
He waits with both hands open by the wall.

Malik jumps and lifts the orange ball up to the high rim.
Tia stands on the court with her hands still open.

Tia jumps and slaps Malik's orange shirt.
He grins at her.
Rosa claps by the tomato pots, green hose in her hand.

They dribble the orange ball in a small circle by the low wall.
Malik and Tia stay bent over the bounce.
The ball keeps tapping the warm cement.

A brown puppy bumps the orange ball with its nose.
The ball sits in a tomato pot.
Rosa smiles and holds her green hose.
A striped skunk stands in the flowers, and yellow waves curl around it. The fox backs away. The dog does too.
The skunk faces the dog on the dirt path and lifts its tail straight up. Yellow waves hang between them. The dog pulls back.
Then the skunk walks off, tail down. The dog sits and rubs one eye with its paw.
A stink bug sits alone on a green leaf. Its brown back looks like a little shield, and yellow waves float up from it.
A millipede curls tight on a stick. Yellow waves roll out, and a bird hops backward.
A hoopoe with a tall crest perches by a hole in the tree. Yellow waves drift out of the dark hole. Down on the ground, a snake turns its head away.
In the woods, a shaggy wolverine rubs against a fallen log. Yellow waves rise from its rear.
Someone holds a small dark turtle up over the creek. Yellow waves puff out all around the turtle.
A coyote walks right past the skunk. Yellow waves curl around the skunk, and the coyote heads toward two little mice in the grass.
A skunk walks the sidewalk. A person in a blue jacket stays well back, with both hands in their pockets.
A millipede curls on a stick, and a stink bug sits on a leaf beside it. Yellow waves rise from both of them.
Nothing is on the path now, but a yellow cloud still hangs over the dirt. The coyote turns and walks away.
The skunk stands in the grass with its tail up. A long yellow arc shoots out and hits a tree.
A long white ticket ribbon spills off the counter and curls around the cook's black boot. He stares down at the loop. That is a lot of lunch.
At the park, a food-truck cook flips burgers on a hot grill. People stand in a line and wait for their turn.
In the school kitchen, a cook spoons beans onto a row of trays. Kids slide the trays along and reach for forks.
A pizza baker slides a pie into the glowing oven on a wooden peel. Flour dusts the counter, and the heat hits her face.
A deli worker pulls a long knife across a turkey and stacks thin slices for a sandwich. A customer taps the glass.
A bakery worker spreads butter on warm rolls, adds ham, and wraps the sandwiches. He sets them in a box on the counter. The clock on the wall ticks.
In the hospital kitchen, a cook sets lids on plates of mashed potatoes. A metal cart waits by the door.
A rider with black bags on his bike weaves past a bus. He pedals toward the shop door.
Steam fogs the small window. A dishwasher turns a heavy wet pot so the last drop can fall in. Racks roll into the steel machine.
A server sets bowls of soup by the window and fills a water glass. A baby bangs a spoon. The family smiles.
A grocer stacks red apples in a wide bin and wipes the wet grapes beside them. Shoppers fill their bags nearby.
Pans hiss, and tickets hang in a row. One worker cooks, one carries plates, and one washes dishes. A mop leans by the back door.
One ticket still hangs on the wheel above a dark burner. The shop is quiet.
The crunch cart rolls down a sunny sidewalk by the park. Bright orange carrots stand in a dented tin cup. The wheels squeak, and then a carrot snaps.
Kids lean close to the cart and listen. It is a loud little snack shop. A small baby covers both ears.
A kid in a yellow shirt bites a raw orange carrot beside the cart. Teeth press down, and the carrot cracks.
A kid in a light blue shirt bites a red apple, and juice sprays out. A bag of small apples sits on the cart.
Two hands snap a slice of toast over the cart. A cloud of crumbs falls onto the carrots.
Two kids laugh and pull long strings from bitten celery sticks. The strings stretch between their fingers.
Two kids stack pale cucumber slices like little wheels. One kid bites a slice while the other adds one more.
A small pile of pretzels sits next to a full bag on the cart. Salt sparkles on the twists, beside the carrots and cucumber slices.
Hands snap green peppers and red peppers over the cart. The pieces open, and seeds bounce across the top.
A freckled kid with curly hair smiles and bites a hard orange carrot. The crunch is right up close.
A wide plate on the picnic table holds carrots, apple slices, toast bits, and cucumber wheels. Two kids reach in for a snack.
Pink gum and sticky candy sit beside leftover carrots on the cart. The sweets look soft. The carrots still look ready to crunch.
The crunch cart rolls past the park gate and down a new street. Orange carrots lean as a wheel bumps a stone.
A gull grabs a warm bun off the harbor dock and flies over the wet ropes. The bell rings. A slow gray boat waits near the pilings.
Workers coil thick ropes and check the wood. Crates of fish crowd the boards, and the air smells salty. A painted arrow points to the ferry slip.
Cars wait in a line by the wide ferry ramp. The gate is up. People walk on and hold the cold rail, and kids wave at the water.
At the fish pier, silver scales flash in pans of ice. A seller slaps a fish on the board and laughs at the splash. Gulls wait on the roof.
A path leads to the rocky point. Thick fog rolls around the lighthouse, and its bright beam turns so boats can miss the sharp reef. A bell rings in the wet air.
A beach ramp slopes into the small waves. A family slides a small boat down the wet boards. A sign shows the tide times so the boat is not left stuck.
Upriver, a quiet wooden dock hugs the bank. Canoes bump the mossy posts after a long, hot paddle. People rest, fill their water bottles, and read a brown trail map.
Green water fills the canal lock, like a slow elevator for boats. The gates are open, and a long barge slides through. Kids count the wet iron rungs.
At night, yellow oil lamps glow over the docks. Boats rock, and a late bell warns a tug in the channel. Cats hunt fish scraps near the wet nets.
Wind kicks spray across the open pier. People leave the pier and wait inside the shed. A dock worker ties extra rope on the posts as the night tide climbs.
Houses lean over the water street. Nets dry on the rails, and kids skip between the fat bollards. Warm light glows in the windows at dusk.
A drawbridge splits the dock street. A tall mast comes through, and the road lifts like a jaw. Walkers wait and eat pretzels. Cars line up in a quiet row.
The evening ferry pulls away from the harbor and heads for the town on the hill. A white wake trails behind it. Lights glow on the docks and on the far slope.
A red cap lifts off a child's head and flies down the street. Leaves and paper race along with it. The cap heads straight for the shop door.
Leaves tumble along the city sidewalk. Flags snap on the poles, and a loose paper slides the same way. A child in a blue coat walks through all that blowing clutter.
On wash day, the shirts kick and the socks twist on the line. A grown-up and a child clip the wet clothes tight. The pins hold on while the wind tries to take the laundry down the yard.
Big trees bend, but they stay in the ground. Twigs snap off and land on the park path. A child steps over them, and a small dog walks right beside.
Up on the grassy hill, a child and a grown-up hold the kite strings. Their feet stay planted in the grass. A red kite and a blue kite dance high while the wind tugs.
An umbrella pops inside out and looks like a bowl. The person in the yellow coat laughs and holds the silly shape. Next to them, another person keeps a folded umbrella close.
At the harbor, boats tug at the ropes on the dock. Flags snap on the poles. Gulls tip their wings and ride the wind over the water.
The kids hold their caps with one hand and their bags with the other. A loose paper flies past and slaps the shop window. The wind keeps the whole street busy.
A farmer slides the latch across the wooden gate. Wind bends the tall grass and pulls at the gate. A goat waits near the open barn door.
The wind dries the shirts on the line. It spins a small pinwheel in the garden. On the wide blue lake, it pushes a sailboat along.
Cans roll through the windy alley. A trash lid bangs and spins above the can. Two kids pick up the light trash and set the lid back on.
At dusk the wind slows down. The caps sit still on the kids' heads. They zip their coats to the chin and walk toward the warm houses.
The night turns sharp and cold. On the window glass, a white frost picture begins to grow. Everyone sleeps inside, where the light stays warm.

Farm workers in straw hats stand at a sunny table and press green stickers onto bananas. Crates of green bananas wait in the field behind them. A ripe yellow banana lies in front, already wearing its sticker.
Two workers load crates of yellow bananas onto a red pickup. The truck sits in wet mud, and one worker is up in the bed.
Beside the tracks, the red pickup meets a green freight car. Two workers pass a crate of green bananas in through the open door.
The train rolls past green fields, a river, and a town with red roofs. A worker in a straw hat fastens the latch on a blue freight-car door.
Gulls fill the sky over the dock. A crane lifts a white container toward a cargo ship. Crates of bananas, oranges, and apples wait on the wooden dock.
The ship cuts through tall waves. Three sailors in hard hats and orange life vests walk the wet deck and hold the rail. Containers stay chained on board.

A cargo plane waits with its nose up and the ramp open. An orange tug pulls a pallet of oranges and other fruit across the pavement toward the plane. Trucks wait nearby, and boats sit on the water by the city.

A big cargo plane crosses the sky above a bay and a city, where a red bridge spans the water. On the hill below, a worker in a hard hat and an orange vest stands by a parked box truck, hands in his pockets.

Night shows through the warehouse door. A forklift carries a tall stack of fruit crates under the bright lights. A blue truck waits at the doorway, back open and taillights on, already loaded with more crates.
A green van is parked up the street from a fruit shop with a striped awning. A cargo bike stands at the curb with a box of fruit. A person in a yellow jacket carries one crate to the shop door.
A hand in a green sleeve sets yellow bananas into a wide bowl. One banana wears a green sticker with a white leaf. A child in a yellow cardigan points at the bowl and laughs.

A red pickup, a steam train, a ship at the dock, a small plane, and a bicycle with a cargo box all share one wide countryside. A rider pedals the bike. A cow grazes, and a chicken keeps a little chick by the fence.
A loose banana rolls across the shop floor toward the open door, and its green sticker shows. A wooden ramp lies in the doorway. Outside, a bicycle holds a crate of leafy greens.
A cart rolls up to the checkout. A big cereal box rides on top, with black dots lined along its side. The clerk leans in so the scanner can see those dots.
The clerk aims a handheld scanner at a box of dry pasta. The scanner beeps, and the price pops up on the small screen.
Look close. Black stripes run along a box, and a small square sits on a paper cup. You can see two kinds of code, side by side.
At the library desk, a worker scans the sticker on a thick picture book. A calendar glows on the computer. A child and a grown-up wait to take the book home.
A little stand on the cafe table holds a square, right by the salt. Someone points a phone at it. The screen opens a menu with soup, warm bread, and sweet tea.
A square sits on the zoo sign by the lions. A grown-up holds a phone still and scans it, while a child watches. A lion rests behind the fence.
At the door of a packed bus, a rider holds up a square on a phone. The box beside the driver beeps. Then the rider can come aboard and sit.
A museum ticket has black stripes along its white side. A guard scans the ticket at the tall glass doors. Beyond them, a hall of dinosaur bones waits for the class.
Shoppers wait in line while coded boxes meet the scanner. Through the big window, a zoo sign shows a square beside the lions.
Someone has taped a square to a street pole. A child points at it, and a grown-up shakes their head. Ask a grown-up before you scan a strange square like that.
A child holds the pasta box steady with both hands. Now the clerk can see the dots and scan them. The shoppers in line wait for their turn.
A paper cup, a library book, and a folded ticket sit together on the kitchen counter. Each one shows a square or a stripe. What will a scanner read the next time you go out?
A tiny tree sits in a square of dirt by the walk. A dog steps right over it, and two people smile at the little green stick.
The tiny tree is a young oak. Sun falls on its leaves, and thin roots run through the cool dirt under the square.
Workers plant young trees along the sunny street. One kneels by a trunk, and another holds a watering can. A wood stake stands beside each little tree.
A green bag of water hugs the thin trunk. Slow drops fall from it, and the dirt by the new roots stays cool and wet.
The bag is empty now. A kid pours water from a can onto the dry dirt, and a bird waits in the next tree.
A rope holds the young oak to the stake. The wind bends the weeds, but the thin trunk stays straight.
In the park, old trees make a wide roof of shade. Two dogs sleep on the grass, and a baby stroller sits under a big maple.
A woodpecker taps a small hole in a pine. Bugs crawl in the rough bark and the sap.
Far from town, oaks cover a long green hill. Deer walk in the deep shade, and people stay on the dirt path.
A hand pulls back from a thin branch. The young oak keeps its green leaves in the sun.
A white sign stands in the new dirt beside the little tree. A red bike rolls around the square.
The oak is as tall as a red bike now. The dog looks up and cannot step over it. A bee sits on a new leaf.
The oak is still thin and young by the walk. A fat squirrel sits on the wood stake.

Steam fogs the cook's glasses as she stirs.
The orange soup bubbles in a big pot, and she laughs.

A farmer unloads crates of orange squash at the dock.
He holds up a small bell, and the cook waves from the door.

The farmer and the cook push the squash cart through the kitchen door.
One squash sticks out, and they both grin.

A helper peels a squash at the counter.
Cubes of it already steam in the pot.

Warm rolls fill the metal pans.
A man stacks the pans by the open kitchen door.

The cook ladles the hot soup into a tall pot.
She smiles through the steam.

On the lunch line, kids take a bowl of soup, a roll, and a cup of milk.
The worker behind the counter smiles at them.

This girl wants one more roll.
Soup, milk, and a roll are already on her tray, and the worker hands her another.

The kids scrape their trays into a big scrap bin.
Bread and bits of vegetables drop in.

In the quiet kitchen, the cook scrubs the big pot.
Her ladle hangs on a hook, and steam still clouds the windows.

The farmer stacks empty crates beside the truck.
No squash is left in them.

The menu board says chili.
A red bowl of it sends up steam in the picture.

The farmer brings sacks of beans to the dock.
He holds the small bell, and the cook waves from the door.

A kid's hands hold a wet rock by the creek.
A shell print curves across the stone, and the rock grins in the sun.

The grin is a shell print, not a drawn face.
A spiral shell sits in soft mud, and the same curl is set in hard gray stone.

Mud and sand stack up in layers over the shell.
The spiral sits deep in the bank while the creek runs beside the grass.

The shell is gone, but the empty shape stays.
Hands hold the gray rock, and the hollow print still grins.

A sea cliff holds a fish print, with fins and a tail still clear.
Waves hit the rocks below, and two gulls fly past the wet stone.

On a grassy hill, hands split a flat stone in two.
A leaf print shows inside, and the veins are thin and neat.

Dry ground under a hot sun holds a long, curved bone.
It lies in pale rock and looks like a giant rib.

Workers in hats chip the dry rock with small tools.
One lifts a print out, and an open box waits, lined with soft padding.

In a big hall, glass cases keep a fish, a leaf, and a curved bone.
The little grin rock sits in a case of its own.

Most of these rocks are plain.
Hands check a row of gray stones on the table, and only one shows a shell print.

A shell sits in wet mud, a fish swims in blue water, and a leaf falls through the air.
Then their three prints rest together in the stone.

A road cuts through a hard hill.
In the rock wall, a huge tree shows ring after ring.

A hammer taps the wet mud by the creek.
A tiny shell pops out, and another little shell rolls toward the water.

A glass jar has tipped under the stove.
Buttons spill and roll on the dark floor.
An orange cat bats a red one with its paw.
A cream shirt lies beside them, missing a button.

A family sews at a wooden table by the oil lamp.
A woman pulls a needle through the cloth.
A man sits close and watches her work.
A child drops buttons into a clear glass jar.

Hands sort buttons on a cloth-covered table.
Wood, shell, and bone mix with bright plastic.
Red, blue, green, and yellow disks shine in the pile.
All of them slide toward a glass jar.

Dad patches the worn knee of a pair of pants.
Grandma holds two small tins of thread.
A needle and a thimble wait on the table.
He sews the rip so the pants can be worn again.

A tailor marks a suit with white chalk.
The cloth lies flat on his shop table.
Bolts of fabric fill the shelves behind him.
Those chalk lines show the shape he will cut.

Three kids wear coats a size too big.
Sleeves hang long, but the buttons still hold.
A grown-up turns a collar and shows a stitched name.
That name marks whose coat this is.

Store shirts hang on hangers along a rack.
A glass jar of buttons sits right beside them.
One white plastic button has a chip along its edge.
The jar is the home supply, next to the new shirts.

Two kids crawl across the rug, hunting a button.
One reaches under a chair, and one looks along the floor.
A tabby cat sits on the chair and watches them.
The button jar waits on a table nearby.

Look at the old photo on the wall.
Three kids stand very still in thick, long coats.
Buttons shine down the front in a row, like little moons.
The picture has faded to brown, and nobody moves.

A school shirt hangs next to a blue jacket.
Bright buttons run down the front of the shirt.
On the jacket, the zipper has stopped halfway.
The shirt can button. The jacket cannot zip.

A grown-up and a child kneel in a closet.
They open an old glass jar packed with buttons.
Light slants through the door, and dust floats in it.
The child leans close for a better look.

Buttons cover a towel, sorted into colors.
A white shirt lies beside them with one button missing.
Rust-colored thread is already in the needle.
One spare button sits ready to sew back on.

After lunch, kids rush into the sunny yard.
A red ball pops off the brick wall.
A jump rope slaps the dry dust.
A ball and a rope are enough to start.

In Ghana, two kids clap and leap in the yard.
One picks a foot and jumps.
The other matches that same foot.
Friends laugh when the feet line up.

In China, kids turn a long rope on the playground.
One friend jumps in time with the swing.
The others wait close by for a turn.
The rope keeps moving, and so does the jumper.

In Brazil, barefoot kids chase a soft ball down a narrow street.
They shout after every kick.
Two shoes sit on the stones, with a bag between them.
That bag is the goal.

In Korea, kids kick a paper shuttlecock in a courtyard.
It must not touch the dusty ground.
Knees bend, and the shuttle dips.
Then it rises again.

In Australia, kids slap a small ball at a school wall.
The ball comes back fast and low.
They hop and tap it with an open palm.
Recess is all bounce.

In Morocco, kids hop through chalk squares on a sunny lane.
A small stone leads the way.
The hopper stays inside the lines.
Friends clap from the side.

In the Philippines, kids stand in a tight dusty circle.
They kick a light woven ball and keep it up.
Ankles flick it from one player to the next.
A long rally brings a cheer.

In Mexico, a wooden top spins on the packed dirt.
A string wraps tight around the top.
One kid whips the string, and the top leans.
The others shout as it spins.

Two kids sit on bare ground and roll a sock into a ball.
A leftover rope lies coiled beside it.
No store toy is in sight.
They can make the rules themselves.

Kids wait in a line for a turn at the game.
One player misses, and friends still cheer.
The next kid steps up.
They wait, miss, and try again.

The sun slides down the school wall.
Dust and small scrapes show on their knees.
Parents call from doors and gates.
The red ball rolls under a low bush.

The kids carry the rope and the red ball home.
The school yard behind them is quiet and gold.
Their legs are tired and dusty.
The street games are done for the day.
Asha waits in the lunch line with an orange tray in both hands. She looks down at the empty tray. Kids stand ahead of her, and the rice, greens, and red fruit sit far up at the counter.
The cook in the tall white hat spoons rice from a big pot. Asha stands still in the line and watches. She holds her tray and waits for her turn.
Nico stands at the edge of the playground. He holds up one finger and counts the kids on the red swings. Three kids are swinging, and one red swing hangs empty.
Nico sits on a red swing and holds both chains. He kicks the dirt, and a puff of dust rises by his shoe.
Priya rocks from foot to foot beside the silver water fountain. A boy in a blue shirt drinks for a long time. Water drips on his shirt, and a drop falls by Priya's white shoe.
Priya leans over the fountain and drinks. She smiles as the water runs. A boy waits behind her with his hands on his hips.
Ben stands outside the blue bathroom door and holds his knees together. A girl and a boy wait in front of him. Ben looks at the yellow sign on the wall.
Ben holds the bathroom door open and smiles. A girl with a ponytail steps inside. A boy at the sink washes his hands.
Kids line up at the teacher's desk. Nico stands in front of Asha. Asha holds her ripped paper in both hands and looks at the tear. The teacher staples a page on the desk.
Kids sit on the green rug and wait to talk. Ben sits with his legs crossed and speaks, one hand up. Priya holds her hand high and listens.
The bus line snakes beside the fence. Kids wear backpacks and wait on the sidewalk. Nico looks down at a crack by his shoe. The yellow bus door is open, and the first kid climbs on.
Asha slides over on the green bus seat and smiles. Her pink backpack sits beside her. A boy with a big blue backpack sits down next to her.
At home, a boy waits for the bathroom. He sits on the floor and stacks red, yellow, and blue cups. His sister sings behind the shower curtain, and a toothbrush rests by the sink.
Three kids stand under a street lamp with backpacks on. Asha is at the front and looks down the empty street. The bus stop sign is there. The bus is not here yet.
Yuki washes a red cup at the kitchen sink. The water rises too high, spills over the rim, and splashes the floor by her blue socks.
Dad runs in from the hall with a towel. "Turn it off!" he calls. Yuki turns the tap off. A wide puddle shines by the white fridge, and Koma stands in the doorway to watch.
Koma comes in from the hall in yellow rain boots. He marches toward the puddle by the white fridge. Yuki watches him from the sink.
Koma looks at the water with wide, worried eyes. His yellow boots squeak on the floor. Yuki grabs a sheet of paper from the mail on the dry end of the table.
Yuki folds the paper into a boat on the dry end of the table. She sets it on the puddle, and it floats right beside Koma's yellow boot. Koma laughs and claps.
Dad mops a path toward the hall doorway. Yuki wades across the shiny puddle with a towel bunched in her hands.
A thick photo book sits on a low stool by the hall. Yuki lifts it with both hands, up off the wet floor. Koma stands beside her in his yellow boots.
Yuki and Koma fold paper boats together at the kitchen table. Three little boats sit near the puddle. Koma smiles at every one.
A paper boat bumps Koma's yellow boot, and he wobbles. Yuki catches his elbow and holds him steady. Dad wrings the towel over the sink, and the big puddle is nearly gone.

Dad wrings the towel into the sink again. Yuki pushes the last of the water toward the sink with a cloth. Koma keeps his yellow rain boots on and pushes a paper boat across the thin puddle by the white fridge.
Yuki opens the photo book on the dry table. She shows Koma baby Yuki in this same kitchen. The floor in the picture is dry, and baby Yuki has no boots on. Koma grins.
They find a photo of Dad as a little boy in huge yellow boots. Dad laughs behind them, mop still in his hand. Koma smiles at the boots in the picture.
Mochi the gray cat sniffs a paper boat on the last puddle by the fridge. Yuki holds still by the table. Koma leans on the table and watches.
Mochi slaps the boat with one fast paw. Water sprays up. The boat spins away toward the white fridge, and Yuki and Koma jump back.
Luis waits in left field on the brown dirt, green cap low and brown glove open. Dust marks the knees of his gray pants. Ana stands just behind him in the same green jersey, her glove ready.
A white ice cream truck rolls by the snack fence. A loud song pours from the speaker on its roof. Luis turns to look at the truck, and the batter swings.
The ball sits in the grass by Luis's feet. He is still watching the truck. Ana sits on the dirt with both hands over her ears.
Luis runs across the brown dirt to Ana. She stays on the ground with her ears covered. The loud song still comes from the truck.
Coach Kim claps from the wood bench by the snack fence. Luis taps Ana's glove and points at home plate. Ana stands, and she looks at the white truck.
The truck is farther down the street. Luis bends his knees and lifts his glove, and Ana does the same. The batter swings, and the ball leaves the bat.
The fly ball comes to left field. Luis catches it in his brown glove. Ana taps his green cap and grins.
A ground ball rolls to Ana on the dirt. She bends low and scoops it into her glove. A runner is still racing, and Luis is right behind her.
Coach Kim waves from the bench, and Luis jogs in. Ana leans on the snack fence and takes a sip of water. The green caps sit in a row.
The truck stops by the snack fence. The driver leans out with a box of red popsicles. Luis and Ana look up at him.
They sit on the bench in their green jerseys. Luis hands Ana a cold red popsicle. She smiles, with one hand over her ear.
A red popsicle slips from the box and falls into Luis's glove. Ana laughs, and her own popsicle tips toward the dirt. The driver looks back from the window.
The driver waves, so Luis and Ana walk to the window. Kids from the other team line up behind them in blue and red. Luis still has his glove on.
The driver sets a tiny paper cap on the popsicle in Luis's glove. Ana holds a paper cap of her own and smiles. They stand together at the open window.
Here is a heap of sticks, dry grass, and mud on the riverbank. That messy pile is a building kit.
Two beavers haul a young log through the pond toward a pile of sticks. One holds the log in its mouth, and the other pushes from behind.
A beaver presses wet mud into the cracks of the stick lodge. Twigs rest in the water right beside it.
A yellow weaver bird ties long grass around a thin branch. He knots it over and over, and the nest starts to hang like a bag.
The grass nest hangs finished, like a woven bag. A small round door sits near the bottom.
A stickleback is a small fish with sharp spines. He works in a pit in the sand, gluing bits of plant with a thread from his own body.
A second fish comes near the sand nest. The male stickleback chases it away.
In the dry desert, a huge mound of sticks rises up. Cactus spines poke from the walls of a packrat's house.
A caddisfly larva lives in a case of sand, twigs, and tiny shells. It drags that little house along the rocks in the stream.
A harvest mouse's nest is a round ball of grass on a tall stem. It sits up above the wet ground.
Side by side, these homes do not match. A beaver lodge sits in the water, a grass bag hangs from a branch, and a grass ball rests on a stem.
A pile of dead sticks lies on the bank beside the pond. Across the water, the beaver lodge is still standing.
Big sticks are stacked into a deep nest on a tall pole. That pile belongs to an osprey.
Look inside the lodge. A dry room sits above the water, and the door is a tunnel that opens under the pond.

A bright lamp hangs over the dock.
A seagull lifts a sandwich from an open crate and flaps away over the dark water.
Two workers grab the wet ropes.

Two workers in yellow hats guide a heavy crate down from the crane.
They hold thick yellow ropes.
The crate hangs over the black water, and a ship sits in the dark behind them.

A night guard walks the wet planks beside a tied boat.
He checks a thick rope and holds a small pad.

In a dark shop, a baker mixes dough in big bowls.
Flour covers her arms.
Pans wait on the cold counter.

In a quiet hall, a night nurse checks a chart with a small light.
She helps a man sit up and sip water.

A street cleaner drives a slow truck.
Brushes spin on the dark street, and water sprays the curb.
A cat runs from a trash can.

In a small booth, a radio host speaks into her mic.
A red light glows on it.
She wears headphones, and the window behind her is dark.

At the press, a worker feeds wide paper into the machine.
Stacks of newspapers pile up beside him.

A night bus stops under a lamp.
The driver shuts the door.
A few riders sit inside.

In a warehouse, night workers scan boxes on a belt.
They load the boxes into a truck.
One worker pulls a box off the belt.

Under a deck light, a fisher mends a net.
Fish slap in a bin.
Gulls wait on the rail, and the boat rocks beside the dock.

A cleaner pushes a wide mop down a bank hall.
He waves at the night guard by the glass doors.

Dock workers coil thick yellow ropes.
A baker slides pans into the oven.
A nurse checks a chart with a small light.
A press worker stacks the newspapers.

A work lamp lights the empty dock.
The crane hook hangs over the black water.
A gull sleeps on the post.

A wide straw basket sits empty on the stones of a busy morning market. Fish gleam on ice down the lane. Round loaves are stacked at another stall, and crates hold cut watermelon, pineapple, and yellow fruit. Shoppers carry baskets from one stall to the next.
Silver fish lie on a bed of crushed ice. The seller laughs and reaches in with one hand. Cold water sprays up around the fish.
Dark greens stand in a straw basket, still wet from the rain. Drops bead on the leaves and on the stone ledge. A hand in a green sleeve holds the bunches steady.
A boy tips a sack, and brown beans rattle into a tin scoop. The scoop fills fast. Extra beans spill across the blue counter.
Warm loaves sit in a long row, and steam rises off the crusts. The baker taps one loaf with his finger. A shopper in round glasses leans close to look.
Oranges are heaped in a wooden bin, with apples tucked beside them. One orange rolls toward a baby stroller. The kid inside stops it with one shoe.
Brown eggs fill a cardboard tray. A girl lifts a cream cloth printed with small red flowers and holds it over the eggs.
A shopper kneels and grips a heavy sack of rice. A hole has opened in the side. White grains pour out, miss the basket of greens, and pile up on the stones.
Red tomatoes rest in a shallow tray, green stems still on. One tomato has split open beside them. Juice and seeds leave a wet stamp on the wood.
Two shoppers smile and hold one big basket between them. Fish, a bowl of beans, round bread, and a tomato pack it full. Loose beans scatter on the cobbles, and another tomato lies on the ground.
A large clay jug stands on a market table. A child drinks from a small clay cup. A woman in a pink scarf drinks from a cup just behind him.
A cook stirs a wide pan over a bright flame. Rice, chopped greens, and small whole fish turn together in the heat. Steam curls up above the stall.
Two kids walk the market lane with baskets of their own. The girl carries cut fruit. The barefoot boy carries round loaves of bread. They smile at each other as they go.
By dusk, the heavy straw basket rests on the steps by a wooden door. Greens, a mound of white rice, and brown roots fill it. The window glows, and lamps are already lit down the street.

Red paper lanterns glow over the night fruit stall.
A seller lifts a yellow mango into that light, and it shines like a little moon.
Crates below spill over with grapes, pomegranates, and lychees.

Mist still hangs on the farm street, and the sky is only just pale.
A man in the back of a truck passes a crate of leafy greens to a woman at the table.
A child in a yellow hat crouches for a tomato on the stones, while steam curls off a tray of sweet buns.

Inside the long hall, cheese wheels sit beside round loaves of bread.
The baker smiles and sets his hand on a big flour-dusted crust.
Shoppers walk the aisle, and the ceiling fans turn slowly overhead.

Boats crowd together on the bright river.
A woman in a conical hat holds out a tied sack, and the man in the next boat takes it, his other hand on a long pole.
A girl sits beside him with both hands on a basket.
Gray fish slip through the water under the boats.

Red, gold, and brown spices fill the open sacks along the brick alley, and strings of chilies hang above them.
A shopper presses a white cloth to their nose.
The seller holds out a little cup of water, and a hanging scale waits with its pan full.

Pans, coils of rope, and boxes of nails cover the sunny hardware stall.
A farmer in a straw hat grips a hoe and tries the wooden handle in both hands.
Beside him a grinding wheel throws sparks.
At the counter, coins pass from hand to hand.

Three children sit at a side table and hold up shiny cards of cats.
One shows a gray kitten, and one shows an orange kitten, with more cats waiting in the tray.
Their parent stands just behind them, hands in her pockets.

Rain falls on the night market, and the red lanterns shine on the wet stones.
People in hoods and coats crowd under the dry stall.
A seller bends over the crates and draws the fruit back from the rain, while umbrellas bob farther down the lane.

Snow lies on the wooden shed, but inside the stove glows.
Red mittens hold up a jar of dark jam and a jar of golden honey.
People clap, and a white-bearded fiddler plays in the warm corner.

The rush is over, and the lane gets a sweep.
One woman brushes yellow peels into a bin, and another sorts scraps beside green glass bottles.
A gray cat and an orange cat sit by a bowl of little fish, waiting on the bits.
A man reaches into a crate of oranges down the row.

The whole market shares one street in the low golden light.
A child in a yellow hat reaches for a tomato by the crates of greens and steaming buns.
Shoppers carry bags past a great wheel of cheese.
At the water's edge, a wooden boat sits loaded with sacks and baskets.

A fruit stall stands under a striped awning, right beside the train station.
The seller holds an orange high over the apples and grapes.
Travelers roll their suitcases and keep small paper tickets in their hands.
The yellow and green train sends up a puff of white smoke.

The market climbs a steep stair of stone above a valley of cloud.
Baskets of lemons sit bright in the sun.
On the wall, a child holds one lemon and looks up at the woman beside them, while an older man rests with his hands in his lap.

The night stall is quiet.
Hands cradle a yellow mango over a wooden crate, and red lanterns hang above the stacked crates and bare boards.
Stone steps climb into the fog, where a small cart waits with a bell on its frame.

Morning light fills the bedroom window.
A thick white picture covers the glass.
It looks like ferns and tiny trees.
No one drew it.
Cold air made the frost while the room stayed warm.

Out in the yard, the frost is thin ice.
It clings to the grass, the bushes, and the car roof.
Dawn light makes it sparkle.
A clear, cold night left it on everything it could reach.

By the front door, the kids pull on two thick socks first.
Then come warm pants, a shirt, a sweater, a coat, and a hat.
Gloves go on once the zippers are done.
Layer by layer, they turn into warm bundles.

On the front steps, each breath turns into a little cloud.
Warm air from their mouths meets the cold and shows up white.
The kids puff, laugh, and rub their cold noses.
Then they start down the steps.

The stone steps look wet, but they are ice.
A boot can slide if someone rushes.
The kids hold the rail.
Salt scattered on the walk is already helping the ice melt.

The pond looks hard under a shining sheet of ice.
The middle is darker, and that ice can still be thin.
The kids stay on the bank and toss a stick.
They keep their boots on the snow.

Snow falls in soft flakes over the hill.
It covers the parked cars and the dark roofs.
The kids drag sleds up through the deep spots.
Their boots sink, so they walk like ducks,
and their hats pick up white crowns.

A plow pushes snow into a long white pile by the curb.
The shop owner scrapes the walk so people can reach the door.
Inside the warm shop, the kids stamp the cold out of their feet.

Fresh snow holds a quiet set of tracks.
Bird feet make thin arrows.
A rabbit leaves paired hops.
A dog leaves big pads with claw marks.
The kids follow the trail along the fence while the snow is still soft.

The birds fluff their feathers until they look round.
A squirrel eats seeds in the snow.
People have filled a tray, and the birds crowd in.
Puffed up and busy, they eat while the ground stays icy.

By midday, sun hits the glass.
Drops slide down, and the fern picture fades from the edges.
In the warm room, the kids peel off wet hats.
The street outside is still white.

The sun sits higher, and the steps begin to drip.
Ice lets go of the stone in slow drops.
By the door, the coats hang on their hooks.

Icicles hang from the shed and drip when the sun hits them.
Inside, the kids sip warm soup.
Wet boots dry by the door
while the drops keep falling outside.
A boy sits on a wooden park bench in the sun. He pulls a white earbud out of his ear and squeezes his eyes shut. That song was too loud.
Up in the plane, the engines hum. Passengers wear soft headphones over both ears. A movie plays on the seat screen, and the sound stays low.
In class, the kids wear headsets and listen to a story. Their teacher stands by the desks and watches. A bin of extra headsets sits nearby.
The train car is packed. A woman wears one earbud and leaves her other ear open. She listens for the speaker by the doors.
People ride bikes in the gym while a song plays. The coach reaches up to the speaker on the wall and turns the volume knob.
Big soft headphones hang on hooks in a quiet library corner. A child puts a pair on and looks at a folk tale on a tablet.
A parent cooks at the stove while a speaker on the shelf reads a recipe. The pot hisses, so the parent reaches up and pauses the voice.
Earbuds wait in an open case on the desk. Headphones hang on a wall hook. A small speaker sits on the kitchen shelf.
By a bright window, a boy takes his earbuds out. He sits in the quiet light with both ears open.
A boy stands at the curb with one ear free. A bike and a bus are on the street, and he can hear them. His earbud case stays in his pocket.
Three kids sit on the rug around a small speaker. One child covers both ears. Another reaches over and turns the song down.
A red bike rests in the rack by the path. A friend on the grass waves and calls. The boy slides his earbud out.
A speaker in the shop ceiling calls out a price. By the bin of purple grapes, a boy wears one earbud and keeps his other ear open.
The boy sits at his desk by the window. Earbuds, headphones, and a small speaker sit in front of him. He looks at them with both ears free.

A green frog sits on a clear bottle in the creek.
The bottle floats by the tall reeds like a little boat.
Two kids on the bank point at the frog and grin.

One side of the bend is clear as glass.
Stones, sand, a stick, and little fish show through the water.
The other side is brown and thick, and the bottom is hidden.

Cans, cups, and bags snag on wet sticks at the bend.
White foam packs in around the trash.
A duck pecks at a bag caught in the foam.

Broken green glass lies in the sand of the shallow creek.
The sharp bits hide among the grit.
A shoe hangs above the water and does not come down.

A wash pail tips on the muddy bank.
Soapy water slides down and spreads bubbles across the creek.
Little fish rise under the foam.

A thin rainbow film of oil sits on the still water by the reeds.
A duck shakes its feathers.
The oil stays stuck, and the duck cannot shake it off.

Fish hide under the roots along the bank.
Frogs sit on wet stones beside a log.
A heron stands in the shallow water and waits.

People in gloves reach in with long grabbers.
They bag the trash and set the bags by a bin on the path.
The foam looks thinner, and a minnow flashes past a clean rock.

A path runs on the dry dirt above the soft mud.
Nests hide down in the reeds.
One dog stays on a leash on the path, and another dog splashes in the creek.

A pond sits still. A creek runs on. A lake opens wide.
A turtle rests on a log.
A flat stone lies on the path.

Rain runs along the street into the grate by the curb.
Cups and bags sit in the grate with wet leaves.
Water backs up and pools on the road.

After the rain, two hands lift a cup out of the grate.
The dark water starts to move.
A bin waits nearby on the sidewalk.

At dusk the creek looks like glass.
Little fish swim in the bright spots by the log.
Frogs sit in the reeds, and each stone shows on the bottom.

The green frog sits on a wet stone in the shallow creek.
Clear water runs around the stone.
The bottle is gone.
A fat pumpkin rolls down the market lane. A little dog runs after it with its mouth open. Shoppers hop aside and throw their arms up.
The farmer holds the pumpkin by the stem and sets it on the crate. A rope stretches across the front. A girl claps.
A baker in a white hat steadies a brown loaf on a wooden board. Butter sits in a tin, and three kids lean in close.
A woman leans over a crate of books. A boy sits on the rug and looks at a picture of a sailboat.
A firefighter pours water into a boy's cup. Three kids put their hands on a black helmet, and the boy smiles.
At the cheese stall, a woman cuts a pale block. A dad holds two wedges in brown paper, and a girl watches.
By the fountain, a woman sits on a stool and plays the violin. Children stop to listen, and coins drop into a mug.
A woman in a straw hat stamps a map and points down the street. A woman with a backpack and a boy look toward the bus.
A woman reaches for a pot of green seedlings wrapped in paper. A boy holds out two coins, a girl drops one into a tin, and a bee flies by.
Shoppers pack the lane. A woman fills a sack with leafy greens, and a basket holds bread and cheese. An older man pats the little dog. The pumpkin stays in its crate.
A woman in a white apron holds open the book with the sailboat. The boy on the rug reaches for the page.
A woman packs books into a crate. The farmer loops a rope around a pumpkin stem. A child pushes a cart with a big blue water jug.
The violin player kneels by her open case and waves. In the doorway, a man holds a mop, and the hall behind him is lit.
A goat walks off with a rope in its mouth. A little dog stands close, mouth open. A watermelon lies on the stones, a pumpkin sits on a crate, and books rest on the rug.
The first boom shakes the room. A white dog hides under the bed, and the lamp sways on its cord. Out the window, drums and a parade fill the street. A baby in the crib blinks hard.
People run into a dusty street toward the hand drums. Feet stamp, and dust rises. Kids cover their ears. Laundry hangs over the road, and pots sit by the doors.
The drum line turns the corner. Kids clap at the curb. Grandpas lift the little ones so they can see the sticks. A whistle cuts the air.
At dusk, red drums lead a new year walk past the shops. Gold tassels swing by the doors. Cloth lions leap and bow to the beat. Firecrackers pop on the curb.
A carnival band rolls down the hill on wheels. Brass horns join the drums as the sun goes down. Painted kids jump when the bass hits hard. Feathers bounce at their necks.
On the prairie, dancers step in a circle around the arbor. A big drum sounds in the middle, and elders sit in a ring. Fringe on the dresses lifts as the dancers turn.
Neighbors sit outside with bread and bowls of soup. A child taps a metal pot, tap, tap, tap. A jar of honey sits by the bread.
Rowers pull a long boat across a wide river. A drummer at the stern hits the drum. The oars follow, one beat and then the next.
A truck rolls slowly down the street. Speakers in the bed blast a beat, and kids fill the road. Confetti sticks in their hair.
In an alley, a kid builds a drum from a tin can and a stick. Tape holds the top in place. The kid gives the can a tap.
A family walks down the block at night. Lanterns glow farther on, and street drums are already booming. The family heads toward the sound.
The drum line passes the front steps. Kids grin and clap for the drummers. A whistle answers from the line.
The last float goes by. A child bangs a rice pot lid with a spoon. Paper cups roll in the gutter, and the street feels still.
A kid steps into the street and keeps time with a spoon. A dog sits nearby and watches every tap.

Shoes pile up by the blue front door.
A wet boot leans on a dry sandal, and bags sit in the heap.
One child steps inside in rain boots, with a backpack still on.
